source.text: Ὄφελον ἀνείχεσθέ μου μικρόν τι ἀφροσύνης· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνέχεσθέ μου.

records.literal_gloss: Would that you were bearing with me a little something of foolishness; but indeed bear with me.

en.L: I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness. But indeed, bear with me.
en.B: I wish you would put up with a little foolishness from me. Yes, do bear with me.
en.R: I hope you will put up with me while I act a little like a fool. Please be patient with me.

fr.L: Si seulement vous me supportiez dans un peu de folie ! Mais oui, supportez-moi.
fr.B: Je voudrais que vous supportiez de ma part un peu de folie. Oui, supportez-moi donc.
fr.R: J’espère que vous me supporterez pendant que j’agis un peu comme un insensé. S’il vous plaît, soyez patients avec moi.

es.L: Ojalá me {{plural_you:soportaran|soportarais}} un poco de insensatez; pero, en verdad, {{plural_you:sopórtenme|soportadme}}.
es.B: Ojalá {{plural_you:aguantaran|aguantarais}} un poco de insensatez de mi parte. Sí, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} paciencia conmigo.
es.R: Espero que me {{plural_you:aguanten|aguantéis}} mientras actúo un poco como un tonto. Por favor, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} paciencia conmigo.

sw.L: Laiti mngenivumilia kidogo katika upumbavu; lakini kweli, nivumilieni.
sw.B: Laiti mngevumilia upumbavu kidogo kutoka kwangu. Naam, nivumilieni.
sw.R: Natumaini mtanivumilia ninapotenda kidogo kama mpumbavu. Tafadhali nivumilieni.

decisions.choice: foolishness: the senseless talk of a boaster
alternatives: the foolishness of the message of the cross (1 Corinthians 1-3)
decisions.reason: ἀφροσύνης begins the passage that runs to 12:11, in which Paul plays the part of a fool and boasts as his rivals do (11:16-18; 12:11). The word, with ἄφρων ("fool"), means lacking good sense. It is a different word from μωρία and μωρός in 1 Corinthians 1-3, where the cross looks foolish to the world but is God's wisdom. Here the foolishness is Paul's own pretended folly, put on so that he can answer the boasting of others.

decisions.choice: an appeal: do bear with me
alternatives: a statement: indeed you are bearing with me
decisions.reason: ἀνέχεσθέ can be an imperative ("bear with me") or an indicative ("you are bearing with me"). After the wish in the first half, an appeal fits well, and the verb comes back in verses 4, 19 and 20, where the Corinthians bear with the rivals all too easily. Read as a statement, Paul would be saying, with some irony, that they are already doing so.

decisions.choice: I wish: a wish Paul is not sure will be granted
decisions.reason: Ὄφελον introduces a wish (as in 1 Corinthians 4:8 and Galatians 5:12). Paul is not certain that the Corinthians will listen.

decisions.choice: act a little like a fool
decisions.reason: Readable says what the foolishness is: Paul is about to speak as a fool would (m1). "Fool" and "foolishness" are kept through 11:1-12:11 at every level, so the reader can follow Paul's fool's speech.

decisions.choice: la folie, un insensé (every level, through 11:1-12:11, as in 12-13)
decisions.reason: Paul's fool's speech turns on this word family, so it is kept at every level, as the English keeps "fool" and "foolishness". "Insensé" (without sense) matches the Greek and sets up the play with "sensés" in 11:19; "fou" is kept for being out of one's mind (11:23).

decisions.choice: insensatez, insensato (L, B); tonto (R)
decisions.reason: This is not the word for foolishness set against wisdom in 1 Corinthians 1-3, where Spanish says "necedad / necio"; "insensatez / insensato" keeps the two apart and pairs with "sensatos" in 11:19. Readable uses the everyday "tonto", as the English Readable says "like a fool".

decisions.choice: upumbavu, mpumbavu (chapters 11-12)
decisions.reason: Recorded for chapters 11-12. The word is the senseless talk of a boaster (meaning decision). Swahili uses "upumbavu" and "mpumbavu" (foolishness, fool), as Mark 7:22 and Luke 12:20 render these Greek words; "mjinga" is kept for the foolish of Matthew's parables. Swahili 1 Corinthians 1-3 also says "upumbavu" for a different Greek word, so a reviewer may want to keep the two apart.

source.text: ζηλῶ γὰρ ὑμᾶς θεοῦ ζήλῳ, ἡρμοσάμην γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀνδρὶ παρθένον ἁγνὴν παραστῆσαι τῷ Χριστῷ·

records.literal_gloss: I am jealous for you with God's jealousy, for I betrothed you to one husband, a virgin pure to present to the Christ;

en.L: For I am jealous over you with a jealousy of God, for I betrothed you to one husband, a pure virgin to present to {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: My jealousy for you is the jealousy of God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. I have pledged you in marriage to one husband: I mean to bring you to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as a pure virgin bride.
en.R: I care about you with the same jealous love that God has for you. You are like a young woman promised in marriage to one man, and I am like the father who arranged it. I want to bring you to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} pure, as a bride who has kept herself for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone.

fr.L: Car je suis jaloux de vous d’une jalousie de Dieu, car je vous ai fiancés à un seul époux, pour vous présenter au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme une vierge pure.
fr.B: Ma jalousie pour vous est la jalousie de Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}. Je vous ai promis en mariage à un seul époux : je veux vous présenter au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme une fiancée vierge et pure.
fr.R: Je tiens à vous avec le même amour jaloux que Dieu a pour vous. Vous êtes comme une jeune fille promise en mariage à un seul homme, et je suis comme le père qui a arrangé ce mariage. Je veux vous présenter au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} comme une fiancée pure, qui s’est gardée pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul.

es.L: Porque estoy celoso por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con celo de Dios, pues {{plural_you:los|os}} comprometí con un solo esposo, una virgen pura para presentar {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.
es.B: El celo que siento por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es el celo de Dios mismo. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} he prometido en matrimonio a un solo esposo: quiero {{plural_you:presentarlos|presentaros}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} como una novia virgen y pura.
es.R: Me preocupo por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con el mismo amor celoso que Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} tiene. {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} como una joven prometida en matrimonio a un solo hombre, y yo soy como el padre que arregló el compromiso. Quiero {{plural_you:llevarlos|llevaros}} {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} puros, como una novia que se ha guardado solo para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana wivu wangu juu yenu ni wivu wa Mungu, kwa maana niliwachumbia mume mmoja, [ili] niwalete kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama bikira aliye safi.
sw.B: Wivu nilio nao juu yenu ni wivu wa Mungu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Nimewachumbia mume mmoja: nataka kuwaleta kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama bibi arusi aliye bikira safi.
sw.R: Ninawajali kwa upendo ule ule wenye wivu ambao Mungu anao kwenu. Ninyi ni kama msichana aliyechumbiwa na mwanamume mmoja, nami ni kama baba aliyepanga uchumba huo. Nataka kuwaleta kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} mkiwa safi, kama bibi arusi aliyejitunza kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} peke yake.

decisions.choice: God's own jealousy: a protective love that will not share the beloved
alternatives: a godly jealousy, meaning simply a good kind of jealousy
decisions.reason: θεοῦ ζήλῳ is "with a jealousy of God": the jealousy Paul feels is God's own for his people, not envy or suspicion. In the Old Testament God is jealous for his people as a husband for his wife (Exodus 20:5; 34:14; Hosea 2:19-20). Paul shares that jealousy because someone is trying to win the Corinthians away (verse 4).

decisions.choice: betrothal: a binding promise of marriage, made before the wedding
decisions.reason: In Jewish and Greek custom a betrothal was a binding agreement, usually arranged by the bride's father, and the bride was expected to stay pure until she was presented to her husband at the wedding. ἡρμοσάμην ("I betrothed") pictures Paul as the one who arranged the match when he brought the gospel to Corinth; he is the church's father in the faith (1 Corinthians 4:15). The presenting looks ahead to Christ's coming (4:14).

decisions.choice: the church as Christ's bride, as Israel was God's bride
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel the bride of God and call her unfaithfulness adultery (Isaiah 54:5; 62:5; Hosea 2:19-20). Paul applies the picture to the church and Christ, as Ephesians 5:25-27 does. The "pure virgin" is the whole church, and the purity meant is undivided loyalty to Christ, as the next verse says.

decisions.choice: I am like the father who arranged it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture behind "I betrothed you" (m2). Paul may see himself as the father who gives the bride, or more loosely as the one who arranged the marriage.

decisions.choice: a pure virgin bride
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "bride" so that the marriage picture stays clear in one sentence.

decisions.choice: Dios mismo, with no span
decisions.reason: As in 5:20, "mismo" after the noun is an adjective in Spanish and takes no deity_pronoun span, where the English "himself" has one.

decisions.choice: wivu
decisions.reason: In 7:7 the zeal word is "bidii", since "wivu" now means jealousy. Here jealousy is the point: God's protective love that will not share the beloved (meaning decision), so "wivu" is right, as Scripture speaks of God as jealous.

decisions.choice: niliwachumbia (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Kuchumbia" is to arrange a binding engagement before the wedding, the betrothal the meaning decision describes; Paul is the one who arranged it.

source.text: φοβοῦμαι δὲ μή πως, ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐξηπάτησεν Εὕαν ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ, φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἁπλότητος καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος τῆς εἰς τὸν Χριστόν.

records.literal_gloss: I fear but lest somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by the cunning of him, may be corrupted the minds of you from the sincerity and the purity the [one] toward the Christ.

en.L: But I fear that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted [and led away] from the sincerity and the purity that [is] toward {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Yet I fear that, in the way the serpent's cunning tricked Eve, your minds may somehow be spoiled and turned away from simple, pure loyalty to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: But I am worried. Long ago the snake was clever and tricked Eve. In the same way, your minds could be led astray, and you could stop being loyal to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} with a pure and undivided heart.

fr.L: Mais je crains que, d’une manière ou d’une autre, comme le serpent a trompé Ève par sa ruse, vos pensées ne soient corrompues [et détournées] de la simplicité et de la pureté envers le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Pourtant je crains que, de la même façon que la ruse du serpent a trompé Ève, vos pensées ne se corrompent d’une manière ou d’une autre et ne se détournent d’un attachement simple et pur au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Mais je suis inquiet. Il y a très longtemps, le serpent a été rusé et il a trompé Ève. De la même façon, vos pensées pourraient être égarées, et vous pourriez cesser d’être fidèles au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} d’un cœur pur et sans partage.

es.L: Pero temo que de algún modo, como la serpiente engañó a Eva con su astucia, {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} mentes sean corrompidas [y apartadas] de la sinceridad y de la pureza [que es] para con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.B: Pero temo que, así como la astucia de la serpiente engañó a Eva, {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} mentes se corrompan de algún modo y se aparten de una lealtad sencilla y pura {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}.
es.R: Pero estoy preocupado. Hace mucho tiempo, la serpiente fue astuta y engañó a Eva. De la misma manera, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} ser engañados en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de pensar, y {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} dejar de ser leales {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} con un corazón puro y sin divisiones.

sw.L: Lakini ninaogopa kwamba kwa namna fulani, kama vile nyoka alivyomdanganya Hawa kwa hila yake, nia zenu zisije zikaharibiwa [na kupotoshwa] kutoka katika uaminifu wa moyo mmoja na usafi ulio kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Lakini ninaogopa kwamba, kama vile hila ya nyoka ilivyomdanganya Hawa, akili zenu zisije kwa namna fulani zikaharibiwa na kugeuzwa mbali na uaminifu wenu safi usiogawanyika kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Lakini ninaogopa. Zamani za kale nyoka alitumia ujanja akamdanganya Hawa. Vivyo hivyo akili zenu zinaweza kupotoshwa, mkaacha kuwa waaminifu kwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa moyo safi usiogawanyika.

decisions.choice: Genesis 3: the serpent deceiving Eve
decisions.reason: In Genesis 3:1-13 the serpent, the most cunning of the animals, deceives Eve, and she says, "The serpent deceived me" (3:13). Paul continues the picture of verse 2: as Eve was led away from loyalty to God by a clever voice, the church, Christ's promised bride, could be led away by the rivals' persuasive words. In verse 14 he names Satan as the one behind such deception.

decisions.choice: corrupted: spoiled and led away from undivided loyalty
alternatives: simplicity in the sense of naivety
decisions.reason: φθαρῇ means to ruin or corrupt, and it was used of a virgin being seduced, which fits the bridal picture. ἁπλότητος is single-mindedness, a heart that is not divided (the same word as "sincerity" in 1:12 in some manuscripts, and "generosity" in 8:2), and ἁγνότητος is purity. Together they describe a bride's wholehearted faithfulness to Christ.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "and the purity" is included
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have both "the sincerity and the purity", while many others have only "the sincerity", and a few give the two words in the other order. Copyists may have added "purity" from the bridal picture of verse 2, or dropped it because the two similar words stood side by side. The SBLGNT includes it. This description is from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: snake
decisions.reason: "Serpent" is a book word; Readable uses the common word. Literal and Balanced keep "serpent", as Genesis 3 has it.

decisions.choice: le serpent (R)
decisions.reason: English Readable says "snake" in place of the book word "serpent". French "serpent" is the everyday word as well as the word of Genesis 3, so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: uaminifu wa moyo mmoja (L); uaminifu usiogawanyika (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is undivided loyalty (meaning decision). "Unyofu" renders a different word in 1:12, and "ukarimu" (9:11, 13) is this word's sense of generosity, which does not fit here, so Swahili says what the loyalty is.

source.text: εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε, ἢ εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον ὃ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε, καλῶς ἀνέχεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: If indeed for the [one] coming another Jesus preaches whom not we preached, or a spirit different you receive which not you received, or a gospel different which not you accepted, well you put up with [it].

en.L: For if the one who comes preaches another Jesus whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different gospel which you did not accept, you put up with [it] well.
en.B: When anyone turns up and preaches another Jesus than the one we preached, or you take in a spirit unlike the one you received, or a gospel unlike the one you welcomed, you tolerate it splendidly!
en.R: Someone comes to you and tells you about a different Jesus from the Jesus we told you about. Or you accept a spirit that is not the Spirit you received before. Or you accept good news that is different from the good news you believed. And you put up with it so easily!

fr.L: Car si celui qui vient prêche un autre Jésus que nous n’avons pas prêché, ou si vous recevez un esprit différent que vous n’avez pas reçu, ou un évangile différent que vous n’avez pas accueilli, vous le supportez bien.
fr.B: Quand quelqu’un arrive et prêche un autre Jésus que celui que nous avons prêché, ou que vous recevez un esprit différent de celui que vous avez reçu, ou un évangile différent de celui que vous avez accueilli, vous le supportez à merveille !
fr.R: Quelqu’un vient chez vous et vous parle d’un autre Jésus que le Jésus dont nous vous avons parlé. Ou bien vous acceptez un esprit qui n’est pas l’Esprit que vous avez reçu avant. Ou bien vous acceptez une bonne nouvelle différente de celle que vous avez crue. Et vous supportez cela si facilement !

es.L: Porque si el que viene predica a otro Jesús que no predicamos, o {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}} un espíritu diferente que no {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, o un evangelio diferente que no {{plural_you:aceptaron|aceptasteis}}, bien lo {{plural_you:toleran|toleráis}}.
es.B: Cuando alguien llega y predica a otro Jesús distinto del que nosotros predicamos, o {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} un espíritu diferente del que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}}, o un evangelio diferente del que {{plural_you:acogieron|acogisteis}}, ¡lo {{plural_you:toleran|toleráis}} de maravilla!
es.R: Alguien llega y {{plural_you:les|os}} habla de un Jesús diferente del Jesús que nosotros {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos. O {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} un espíritu que no es el Espíritu que {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} antes. O {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} una buena noticia diferente de la que {{plural_you:creyeron|creísteis}}. ¡Y lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}} con tanta facilidad!

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa yule ajaye anamhubiri Yesu mwingine ambaye hatukumhubiri, au mnapokea roho mwingine ambaye hamkumpokea, au Injili nyingine ambayo hamkuikubali, mnavumilia vema [hilo].
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akija na kumhubiri Yesu mwingine tofauti na yule tuliyemhubiri, au mkipokea roho tofauti na yule mliyempokea, au Injili tofauti na ile mliyoikaribisha, mnavumilia hilo vizuri sana!
sw.R: Mtu anakuja kwenu na kuwaambia habari za Yesu tofauti na Yesu tuliyewaambia habari zake. Au mnakubali roho ambaye si Roho mliyempokea mwanzoni. Au mnakubali habari njema tofauti na ile Habari Njema mliyoiamini. Nanyi mnavumilia hayo kwa urahisi sana!

decisions.choice: the one who comes: any visiting teacher of this kind, the rivals
alternatives: a single leader among the rivals
decisions.reason: ὁ ἐρχόμενος is singular, but it most likely stands for whoever comes, the visiting teachers Paul calls false apostles in verse 13. The phrase marks them as outsiders who arrived after Paul had founded the church (10:14-15).

decisions.choice: another Jesus, a different spirit, a different gospel: a false message about Jesus
decisions.reason: The rivals preach a Jesus with a message Paul does not recognize as the gospel. The Corinthians received the Spirit when they believed Paul's preaching (1:21-22; Galatians 3:2), and a different message brings a spirit that is not God's. Galatians 1:6-9 uses the same words, εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον, of a message that is no gospel at all. What exactly the rivals taught is not said; in chapters 10-13 they boast of their status and powers and despise weakness.

decisions.choice: you put up with it well: bitter irony
decisions.reason: καλῶς ("well, finely") is ironic, as in Mark 7:9. The Corinthians are patient with the rivals' false message, though not with Paul (verse 1).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you put up with" (present)
alternatives: "you would put up with" (past tense form)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the verb in a past tense form, which makes the sentence a supposition ("if someone came ..., you would put up with it"); others have the present tense, which says that it is happening. The SBLGNT has the present. This description is from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: you tolerate it splendidly!
alternatives: you put up with it well enough
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the irony of the word "well" (m3).

decisions.choice: a spirit that is not the Spirit you received
decisions.reason: Readable names the Holy Spirit as the Spirit the Corinthians received (m2).

decisions.choice: un évangile différent, lowercase (L, B)
decisions.reason: The capital in "l’Évangile" marks the one message of God; a different gospel preached by the rivals is not that message (m2), so it takes a small letter.

source.text: λογίζομαι γὰρ μηδὲν ὑστερηκέναι τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων·

records.literal_gloss: I consider for in nothing to have fallen short of the super-very apostles;

en.L: For I reckon [that I] have fallen short in nothing of the super-apostles.
en.B: I count myself not one bit behind the super-apostles.
en.R: I do not think those so-called super-apostles are any better than I am.

fr.L: Car j’estime n’avoir été en rien inférieur aux super-apôtres.
fr.B: Je ne me considère inférieur en rien aux super-apôtres.
fr.R: Je ne pense pas que ces soi-disant super-apôtres valent mieux que moi.

es.L: Porque considero que en nada he sido inferior a los superapóstoles.
es.B: Me considero en nada inferior a esos superapóstoles.
es.R: No creo que esos llamados superapóstoles sean mejores que yo.

sw.L: Kwa maana nadhani sijapungukiwa na kitu chochote kuliko mitume wakuu mno.
sw.B: Sijioni kuwa nimepungua hata kidogo kuliko hao mitume wakuu mno.
sw.R: Sidhani kwamba hao wanaoitwa mitume wakuu mno ni bora kuliko mimi.

decisions.choice: the super-apostles: Paul's mocking name for the rivals
alternatives: the leading apostles in Jerusalem, such as Peter, James and John
decisions.reason: ὑπερλίαν is an adverb, "beyond measure, exceedingly", and with ἀποστόλων it makes an ironic title: "the extra-special apostles". Paul uses it again in 12:11. Most likely it means the rivals of verses 4 and 13, who claimed to be apostles of higher standing than Paul, and whom he calls false apostles. Some take it to mean the original apostles in Jerusalem, whom the rivals may have claimed as their backing (compare Galatians 2:6, 9); but Paul would hardly call those men servants of Satan (verses 13-15).

decisions.choice: for: the reason the Corinthians can bear with him
decisions.reason: ὑστερηκέναι is "to have fallen short, to be inferior". The "for" gives the ground for Paul's appeal: he is in no way behind those the Corinthians admire, so they should hear him.

decisions.choice: the super-apostles (L, B); those so-called super-apostles (R)
decisions.reason: "Super-apostles" keeps the mockery of Paul's coined title (m1); a respectful phrase such as "most eminent" would lose it. Readable adds "so-called" to make the irony plain. 12:11 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: les super-apôtres (L, B); ces soi-disant super-apôtres (R), the same in 12:11
decisions.reason: "Super-apôtres" keeps the mockery of Paul's coined title (m1), as the English does; a respectful phrase would lose it. Readable adds "soi-disant" to make the irony plain.

decisions.choice: los superapóstoles (L, B); esos llamados superapóstoles (R)
decisions.reason: Paul coins an ironic word, apostles who are "more than very much" (meaning decision). "Superapóstoles" keeps the irony in one word, as the English "super-apostles" does; Readable adds "esos llamados" to make the irony plain. The same words come back in 12:11.

decisions.choice: mitume wakuu mno (L, B); wanaoitwa mitume wakuu mno (R)
decisions.reason: Paul's mocking name for the rivals (meaning decision): "mitume wakuu mno" (exceedingly great apostles) keeps the overstatement; Readable adds "wanaoitwa" (so-called), as the English Readable does. The same words return in 12:11.

source.text: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδιώτης τῷ λόγῳ, ἀλλ’ οὐ τῇ γνώσει, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ φανερώσαντες ἐν πᾶσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: If but even untrained in the speech, yet not in the knowledge, but in every [way] having made [it] plain in all things to you.

en.L: But even if [I am] untrained in speech, yet [I am] not in knowledge; indeed, in every [way] we have made [this] plain to you in all things.
en.B: Even if I am untrained in speaking, I am not so in knowledge. We have shown you that plainly, in every way and in all things.
en.R: Maybe I am not a skilled speaker, but I do know what I am talking about. We have made that very clear to you in every way.

fr.L: Mais si même [je suis] inexpérimenté en parole, je ne [le suis] pas en connaissance ; au contraire, en tout nous [vous l’]avons montré clairement en toutes choses.
fr.B: Même si je ne suis pas un orateur formé, je ne manque pas de connaissance. Nous vous l’avons montré clairement, de toutes les manières et en toutes choses.
fr.R: Je ne suis peut-être pas un orateur habile, mais je sais de quoi je parle. Nous vous l’avons montré très clairement de toutes les manières.

es.L: Y aunque [sea] inexperto en la palabra, no lo [soy] en el conocimiento; al contrario, en todo [lo] hemos manifestado ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en todas las cosas.
es.B: Aunque sea inexperto en el hablar, no lo soy en el conocimiento. {{plural_you:Se lo|Os lo}} hemos mostrado claramente, de todas las maneras y en todas las cosas.
es.R: Quizás no sea un orador hábil, pero sí sé de lo que hablo. Eso {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} hemos dejado muy claro de todas las maneras.

sw.L: Lakini hata ikiwa [mimi ni] mtu wa kawaida katika usemi, sivyo katika ujuzi; bali katika kila [namna] tumelidhihirisha [hili] kwenu katika mambo yote.
sw.B: Hata kama mimi si msemaji aliyefunzwa, sivyo katika ujuzi. Tumewaonyesha hilo waziwazi, kwa kila namna na katika mambo yote.
sw.R: Huenda mimi si msemaji stadi, lakini ninajua ninachosema. Tumewaonyesha hilo waziwazi kwa kila namna.

decisions.choice: untrained in speech: not a professional speaker
decisions.reason: ἰδιώτης is a layman, someone without professional training in a skill. In Greek cities speakers trained in rhetoric were admired and paid, and Paul's critics said his speech was contemptible (10:10). Paul had chosen not to rely on polished speech (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). He grants the point about his speaking but not about his knowledge of the truth.

decisions.choice: we have made it plain: Paul's knowledge has been shown openly to the Corinthians
alternatives: the truth has been made plain
decisions.reason: φανερώσαντες is a participle with no main verb, and the plural is Paul's "we", himself with his companions or himself alone (1:8). What has been made plain is probably his knowledge, shown in everything he did and taught among them. The sentence is compressed, and the words supplied make it complete.

source.text: Ἢ ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησα ἐμαυτὸν ταπεινῶν ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑψωθῆτε, ὅτι δωρεὰν τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγέλιον εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Or a sin did I commit myself humbling so that you might be exalted, because free of charge the of the God gospel I preached to you?

en.L: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
en.B: Or was it a sin on my part to lower myself so that you could be lifted up, by proclaiming God's gospel to you without charging you anything?
en.R: I made myself low so that you could be lifted up. I told you God's good news and did not ask you to pay me anything. Was that a sin?

fr.L: Ou bien ai-je commis un péché en m’abaissant moi-même pour que vous soyez élevés, parce que je vous ai annoncé gratuitement l’Évangile de Dieu ?
fr.B: Ou bien était-ce un péché de ma part de m’abaisser pour que vous soyez élevés, en vous annonçant l’Évangile de Dieu sans rien vous demander ?
fr.R: Je me suis abaissé pour que vous soyez élevés. Je vous ai annoncé la bonne nouvelle de Dieu sans vous demander de me payer. Est-ce que c’était un péché ?

es.L: ¿O cometí pecado humillándome a mí mismo para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} enaltecidos, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncié gratuitamente el evangelio de Dios?
es.B: ¿O fue un pecado de mi parte rebajarme para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} enaltecidos, al {{plural_you:anunciarles|anunciaros}} el evangelio de Dios sin {{plural_you:cobrarles|cobraros}} nada?
es.R: Me hice pequeño para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} levantados. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} anuncié la buena noticia de Dios y no {{plural_you:les|os}} pedí que me {{plural_you:pagaran|pagarais}} nada. ¿Fue eso un pecado?

sw.L: Au je, nilitenda dhambi kwa kujinyenyekeza ili ninyi mpate kuinuliwa, kwa sababu niliwahubiria Injili ya Mungu bila malipo?
sw.B: Au je, ilikuwa dhambi kwangu kujishusha ili ninyi mwinuliwe, kwa kuwahubiria Injili ya Mungu bila kuwatoza chochote?
sw.R: Nilijishusha ili ninyi mpate kuinuliwa. Niliwaambia Habari Njema ya Mungu, wala sikuwaomba mnilipe chochote. Je, hiyo ilikuwa dhambi?

decisions.choice: preaching free of charge: refusing pay from the Corinthians
decisions.reason: Traveling teachers and philosophers were usually paid fees or supported by wealthy patrons. In Corinth Paul worked at his trade instead (Acts 18:3) and refused support from the church, so that no one could say he preached for money (1 Corinthians 9:12-18). Some Corinthians seem to have taken this as an insult, or as a sign that he was no true apostle (12:13).

decisions.choice: humbling myself: lowering his status by manual work
decisions.reason: ταπεινῶν is to make low. Working with his hands put Paul on the level of a laborer, which people of standing despised (1 Corinthians 4:12). The purpose was that the Corinthians would be raised up through the gospel, as Christ became poor to make others rich (8:9).

decisions.choice: a question full of irony
decisions.reason: Paul asks whether his free preaching was a sin because his critics treat it as one. The answer he expects is no.

decisions.choice: bila malipo
decisions.reason: "Bure" means both "free of charge" and "in vain" (see 6:1), so Swahili says "bila malipo" (without payment), which can only mean that Paul took no pay.

source.text: ἄλλας ἐκκλησίας ἐσύλησα λαβὼν ὀψώνιον πρὸς τὴν ὑμῶν διακονίαν, καὶ παρὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑστερηθεὶς οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐθενός· τὸ γὰρ ὑστέρημά μου προσανεπλήρωσαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας· καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρῆ ἐμαυτὸν ὑμῖν ἐτήρησα καὶ τηρήσω.

records.literal_gloss: Other churches I robbed, having received wages for the of you service, \v 9 and being present with you and having been in need, not I burdened anyone; for the need of me supplied the brothers having come from Macedonia; and in everything unburdensome myself to you I kept and I will keep.

en.L: I robbed other churches, taking wages [from them] for the service of you, \v 9 and when I was present with you and was in need, I burdened no one; for my need the brothers coming from Macedonia supplied; and in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will keep [myself so].
en.B: I plundered other churches, accepting pay from them so that I could serve you. \v 9 And while I was there with you and ran short, I was a weight on no one, for the brothers who came from Macedonia made up what I lacked. In every way I have made sure I cost you nothing, and I will keep it that way.
en.R: Other churches paid me so that I could serve you. It was almost like robbing them! \v 9 When I was with you and needed something, I did not ask any of you for help. The brothers who came from Macedonia brought me what I needed. I have never let myself be a load on you, and I never will.

fr.L: J’ai dépouillé d’autres églises en recevant [d’elles] un salaire pour vous servir, \v 9 et, quand j’étais présent chez vous et que j’étais dans le besoin, je n’ai été à charge à personne ; car les frères venus de Macédoine ont pourvu à mon besoin ; et en tout je me suis gardé de vous être à charge, et je m’en garderai.
fr.B: J’ai pillé d’autres églises en acceptant d’elles un salaire pour pouvoir vous servir. \v 9 Et quand j’étais chez vous et que j’ai manqué de quelque chose, je n’ai pesé sur personne, car les frères venus de Macédoine ont comblé ce qui me manquait. En toutes choses, j’ai veillé à ne rien vous coûter, et je continuerai ainsi.
fr.R: D’autres églises m’ont payé pour que je puisse vous servir. C’était presque comme si je les volais ! \v 9 Quand j’étais avec vous et que j’avais besoin de quelque chose, je n’ai demandé d’aide à aucun de vous. Les frères qui sont venus de Macédoine m’ont apporté ce dont j’avais besoin. Je ne me suis jamais permis d’être une charge pour vous, et je ne le ferai jamais.

es.L: A otras iglesias despojé, recibiendo salario [de ellas] para el servicio a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 9 y cuando estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y tuve necesidad, no fui una carga para nadie; porque lo que me faltaba lo suplieron los hermanos que vinieron de Macedonia; y en todo me guardé de {{plural_you:serles|seros}} una carga, y me guardaré.
es.B: Saqueé a otras iglesias, aceptando de ellas un sueldo para poder {{plural_you:servirles|serviros}}. \v 9 Y cuando estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y me faltó algo, no fui un peso para nadie, porque los hermanos que llegaron de Macedonia cubrieron lo que me faltaba. En todo he procurado no {{plural_you:costarles|costaros}} nada, y así lo seguiré haciendo.
es.R: Otras iglesias me pagaron para que yo pudiera {{plural_you:servirles|serviros}}. ¡Fue casi como robarles! \v 9 Cuando estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y necesitaba algo, no le pedí ayuda a ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Los hermanos que vinieron de Macedonia me trajeron lo que necesitaba. Nunca he sido una carga para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y nunca lo seré.

sw.L: Niliyanyang'anya makanisa mengine, nikipokea mshahara [kutoka kwao] kwa ajili ya huduma kwenu, \v 9 na nilipokuwapo pamoja nanyi na kupungukiwa, sikumlemea mtu yeyote; kwa maana ndugu waliokuja kutoka Makedonia walijaza upungufu wangu; na katika kila jambo nilijilinda nisiwe mzigo kwenu, nami nitaendelea kujilinda [hivyo].
sw.B: Niliyapora makanisa mengine, nikipokea malipo kutoka kwao ili niweze kuwatumikia ninyi. \v 9 Na nilipokuwa huko pamoja nanyi nikapungukiwa, sikuwa mzigo kwa mtu yeyote, kwa maana ndugu waliokuja kutoka Makedonia walinitimizia kile nilichopungukiwa. Kwa kila namna nimehakikisha kwamba siwagharimu chochote, nami nitaendelea hivyo.
sw.R: Makanisa mengine yalinilipa ili niweze kuwatumikia ninyi. Ilikuwa karibu kama kuyanyang'anya! \v 9 Nilipokuwa pamoja nanyi na kuhitaji kitu, sikumwomba yeyote kati yenu msaada. Ndugu waliokuja kutoka Makedonia waliniletea nilichohitaji. Sijawahi kujifanya mzigo kwenu, wala sitafanya hivyo kamwe.

decisions.choice: robbed, taking wages: a soldier's words, used with deliberate exaggeration
decisions.reason: ἐσύλησα means to strip or plunder, as soldiers stripped a defeated enemy, and ὀψώνιον is a soldier's ration money, his pay. Paul says, with mock severity, that he took gifts from other churches, which were themselves poor (8:1-2), so that the Corinthians could have the gospel for nothing.

decisions.choice: the brothers from Macedonia: messengers bringing gifts from the churches there
decisions.reason: Macedonia was the Roman province to the north of Achaia, with the churches of Philippi and Thessalonica. The Philippians sent Paul gifts more than once (Philippians 4:15-16), and Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia while he was in Corinth (Acts 18:5). These brothers were most likely particular men who carried the gift.

decisions.choice: burden: to be a dead weight on someone's resources
decisions.reason: κατενάρκησα is a rare word, used in the New Testament only by Paul (12:13-14). It means to weigh someone down, here by living at their expense. ἀβαρῆ, "not burdensome", says the same thing.

decisions.choice: It was almost like robbing them!
decisions.reason: Readable keeps Paul's word but says that it is an exaggeration (m1).

decisions.choice: brothers, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: The brothers who brought the gift were most likely particular men (m2), so no gender setting is used, as in 8:23.

decisions.choice: niliyanyang'anya, mshahara (L); niliyapora, malipo (B)
decisions.reason: The words are a soldier's, plundering and drawing pay, used with deliberate exaggeration (meaning decision), so Swahili keeps strong verbs: "kunyang'anya" (to rob) and "kupora" (to plunder).

source.text: ἔστιν ἀλήθεια Χριστοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ὅτι ἡ καύχησις αὕτη οὐ φραγήσεται εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τῆς Ἀχαΐας.

records.literal_gloss: Is [the] truth of Christ in me that the boasting this not will be stopped as to me in the regions of the Achaia.

en.L: [As] the truth of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is in me, this boasting will not be silenced as to me in the regions of Achaia.
en.B: I declare by the truth of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} that is in me: this boast of mine will not be silenced anywhere in the districts of Achaia.
en.R: I have the truth of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in me, so I promise you this: no one anywhere in the province of Achaia will stop me from boasting that I preached to you for free.

fr.L: [Aussi vrai que] la vérité du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est en moi, ce sujet de fierté ne sera pas réduit au silence pour moi dans les régions de l’Achaïe.
fr.B: Je l’affirme par la vérité du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} qui est en moi : personne ne m’empêchera de me vanter de cela, où que ce soit dans les régions de l’Achaïe.
fr.R: La vérité du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est en moi, alors je vous le promets : personne, nulle part dans la province d’Achaïe, ne m’empêchera de me vanter de vous avoir annoncé la bonne nouvelle gratuitement.

es.L: [Como] la verdad {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} está en mí, este gloriarme no me será acallado en las regiones de Acaya.
es.B: Por la verdad {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} que está en mí, declaro que nadie me impedirá gloriarme de esto en ninguna parte de la región de Acaya.
es.R: La verdad {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} está en mí, así que {{plural_you:les|os}} prometo esto: nadie en toda la provincia de Acaya me impedirá gloriarme de que {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncié la buena noticia gratis.

sw.L: [Kama] kweli ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ilivyo ndani yangu, kujivunia huku hakutanyamazishwa kwangu katika nchi za Akaya.
sw.B: Ninatangaza kwa kweli ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} iliyo ndani yangu: kujivunia huku kwangu hakutanyamazishwa popote katika wilaya za Akaya.
sw.R: Kweli ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} iko ndani yangu, kwa hiyo nawaahidi hili: hakuna mtu popote katika jimbo la Akaya atakayenizuia kujivunia kwamba niliwahubiria bila malipo.

decisions.choice: a solemn assurance, close to an oath
decisions.reason: "The truth of Christ is in me" is a way of making a solemn statement, as Romans 9:1 ("I am speaking the truth in Christ") and 2 Corinthians 1:18 and 11:31 are. Paul stakes his truthfulness on his belonging to Christ.

decisions.choice: this boasting: his pride in preaching without pay
decisions.reason: καύχησις refers back to verses 7-9: Paul's boast is that he has preached free of charge, as in 1 Corinthians 9:15, where he says that no one will empty his boast. φραγήσεται is "to be stopped up", as a mouth is shut (Romans 3:19).

decisions.choice: Achaia: the Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth its capital
decisions.reason: The letter is addressed to the church in Corinth and to all God's people in Achaia (1:1). Paul will not take support from anyone in the province.

decisions.choice: boast, boasting
decisions.reason: In chapters 10-12 Paul's argument turns on the word itself, so every level keeps "boast" (docs/corinthians-terms.md), where 1:12 has "take pride" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: that I preached to you for free
decisions.reason: Readable says what the boast is (m2).

decisions.choice: ce sujet de fierté (L); me vanter (B, R)
decisions.reason: This boast is a good one, Paul's pride in preaching without pay (m2), so Literal uses "sujet de fierté" for the noun rather than the pejorative "vantardise"; Balanced and Readable turn it into the verb "se vanter", kept at every level in chapters 10-12.

source.text: διὰ τί;

records.literal_gloss: Through what?

en.L: Why?
en.B: Why so?
en.R: Why do I refuse to take your money?

fr.L: Pourquoi ?
fr.B: Pourquoi cela ?
fr.R: Pourquoi est-ce que je refuse de prendre votre argent ?

es.L: ¿Por qué?
es.B: ¿Y por qué?
es.R: ¿Por qué me niego a aceptar {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} dinero?

sw.L: Kwa nini?
sw.B: Kwa nini hivyo?
sw.R: Kwa nini ninakataa kupokea fedha zenu?

decisions.choice: Why do I refuse to take your money?
decisions.reason: Readable says what the question is about, which the verses before make clear.

source.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἀγαπῶ ὑμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Because not I love you?

en.L: Because I do not love you?
en.B: Because I do not love you?
en.R: Is it because I do not love you?

fr.L: Parce que je ne vous aime pas ?
fr.B: Parce que je ne vous aime pas ?
fr.R: Est-ce parce que je ne vous aime pas ?

es.L: ¿Porque no {{plural_you:los|os}} amo?
es.B: ¿Porque no {{plural_you:los|os}} amo?
es.R: ¿Es porque no {{plural_you:los|os}} amo?

sw.L: Kwa sababu siwapendi?
sw.B: Kwa sababu siwapendi?
sw.R: Je, ni kwa sababu siwapendi?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: Some in Corinth may have taken Paul's refusal of their support as a sign that he did not want close ties with them, since accepting a gift created a bond of friendship. Paul raises the charge in order to deny it.

source.text: ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν.

records.literal_gloss: The God knows.

en.L: God knows.
en.B: God knows I do!
en.R: God knows that I do love you!

fr.L: Dieu le sait.
fr.B: Dieu sait que je vous aime !
fr.R: Dieu sait que je vous aime vraiment !

es.L: Dios [lo] sabe.
es.B: ¡Dios sabe que sí {{plural_you:los|os}} amo!
es.R: ¡Dios sabe que de verdad {{plural_you:los|os}} amo!

sw.L: Mungu anajua.
sw.B: Mungu anajua kwamba nawapenda!
sw.R: Mungu anajua kwamba kweli ninawapenda!

decisions.choice: God knows: calling God as witness that he does love them
decisions.reason: Paul calls on God as the witness of what is in his heart, as in verse 31 and 12:2-3. The words answer the question before them: he does love the Corinthians.

decisions.choice: I do; that I do love you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add the answer so that "God knows" is not heard as a shrug (m1).

source.text: Ὃ δὲ ποιῶ καὶ ποιήσω, ἵνα ἐκκόψω τὴν ἀφορμὴν τῶν θελόντων ἀφορμήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καυχῶνται εὑρεθῶσιν καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: What but I do also I will do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those wanting an opportunity, so that in what they boast they may be found just as also we.

en.L: But what I am doing I will also [keep] doing, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who want an opportunity, so that in what they boast [of] they may be found [to be] just as we [are].
en.B: And I will go on doing what I am doing, to deny an opening to those who look for one: an opening to boast that they are on the same footing as we are.
en.R: I will keep on working without pay from you. Those people want a chance to boast that they are just like us. I am not going to give them that chance.

fr.L: Mais ce que je fais, je le ferai encore, afin de couper court à l’occasion de ceux qui veulent une occasion, afin que, dans ce dont ils se vantent, ils soient trouvés tels que nous.
fr.B: Je continuerai à faire ce que je fais, pour ôter tout prétexte à ceux qui en cherchent un : un prétexte pour se vanter d’être sur le même pied que nous.
fr.R: Je vais continuer à travailler sans recevoir d’argent de vous. Ces gens-là veulent une occasion de se vanter d’être comme nous. Je ne vais pas leur donner cette occasion.

es.L: Pero lo que hago, también [lo seguiré] haciendo, para quitar la ocasión a los que quieren una ocasión, a fin de que en aquello de lo que se glorían sean hallados tal como nosotros.
es.B: Y seguiré haciendo lo que hago, para quitarles la oportunidad a los que buscan una: la oportunidad de gloriarse de estar al mismo nivel que nosotros.
es.R: Seguiré trabajando sin que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:paguen|paguéis}}. Esas personas quieren una oportunidad para gloriarse de que son iguales a nosotros. No les voy a dar esa oportunidad.

sw.L: Lakini kile ninachofanya nitaendelea pia kukifanya, ili nikate nafasi ya wale wanaotaka nafasi, ili katika kile wanachojivunia waonekane [kuwa] kama sisi.
sw.B: Nami nitaendelea kufanya ninachofanya, ili niwanyime nafasi wale wanaoitafuta: nafasi ya kujivunia kwamba wako sawa nasi.
sw.R: Nitaendelea kufanya kazi bila kupokea malipo kutoka kwenu. Watu wale wanataka nafasi ya kujivunia kwamba wao ni kama sisi. Sitawapa nafasi hiyo.

decisions.choice: the rivals want to be seen as Paul's equals in the work they boast of
alternatives: Paul refuses pay so that the rivals, who take pay, will be found to be no better than Paul in the matter they boast of
Paul hopes the rivals will be shamed into working without pay as he does
decisions.reason: The second "so that" is hard. Most likely it describes the opportunity the rivals want: to be regarded as Paul's equals in the apostleship they boast of. As long as Paul takes nothing, there is a plain difference between him and them, since they accept support (verse 20; 1 Corinthians 9:12). Other readings take the clause as Paul's own aim.

decisions.choice: opportunity: a base of operations, a pretext
decisions.reason: ἀφορμὴν was a military word for a base from which to launch an attack, and so an opening or pretext (5:12; Romans 7:8). The rivals want something they can use against Paul or in their own favor.

decisions.choice: working without pay from you
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul is doing, from verses 7-9.

source.text: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι ψευδαπόστολοι, ἐργάται δόλιοι, μετασχηματιζόμενοι εἰς ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: The for such [men are] false apostles, workers deceitful, disguising themselves into apostles of Christ;

en.L: For such [people are] false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: People like that are false apostles and dishonest workers, passing themselves off as apostles of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Those people are not real apostles. They are workers who lie to people. They only pretend to be apostles of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Car de tels [gens sont] de faux apôtres, des ouvriers trompeurs, qui se déguisent en apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Ces gens-là sont de faux apôtres, des ouvriers malhonnêtes, qui se font passer pour des apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Ces gens-là ne sont pas de vrais apôtres. Ce sont des ouvriers qui mentent aux gens. Ils font seulement semblant d’être des apôtres du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: Porque los tales [son] falsos apóstoles, obreros engañosos, que se disfrazan de apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.B: Personas así son falsos apóstoles y obreros deshonestos, que se hacen pasar por apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: Esas personas no son verdaderos apóstoles. Son obreros que engañan a la gente. Solo fingen ser apóstoles {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana hao wa namna hiyo [ni] mitume bandia, wafanyakazi wenye hila, wakijibadilisha sura [kuwa] mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Watu kama hao ni mitume bandia na wafanyakazi wasio waaminifu, wanaojifanya kuwa mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Watu hao si mitume halisi. Ni wafanyakazi wanaowadanganya watu. Wanajifanya tu kuwa mitume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: false apostles: people who claim to be sent by Christ but are not
decisions.reason: ψευδαπόστολοι appears only here in the New Testament. An apostle is someone sent with a commission, and Paul's apostleship came from Christ himself (1:1; Galatians 1:1). The rivals claim the same and are not what they claim.

decisions.choice: deceitful workers: teachers at work in the church who use deceit
decisions.reason: ἐργάται was used of those who labor in the gospel (Matthew 9:37-38; 1 Timothy 5:18). δόλιοι means using trickery, as in 4:2, where Paul says he does not use cunning. Compare "the evil workers" of Philippians 3:2.

decisions.choice: disguising themselves: changing their outward appearance
decisions.reason: μετασχηματιζόμενοι is to change the outward form of something, and here to take on a false appearance. Paul uses the verb three times in verses 13-15: the rivals, Satan and Satan's servants all disguise themselves.

decisions.choice: mitume bandia; kujibadilisha sura (L); kujifanya (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Bandia" (counterfeit) says that they claim to be what they are not (meaning decision). Literal keeps the verb of changing one's outward form with "kujibadilisha sura" through verses 13-15; Balanced and Readable say "kujifanya" (to pretend to be).

source.text: καὶ οὐ θαῦμα, αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Σατανᾶς μετασχηματίζεται εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός·

records.literal_gloss: And no wonder, himself for the Satan disguises himself into an angel of light;

en.L: And [it is] no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
en.B: No surprise there: Satan himself passes himself off as an angel of light.
en.R: That should not surprise us. Even Satan makes himself look like a shining angel from heaven.

fr.L: Et [ce n’est] pas étonnant, car Satan lui-même se déguise en ange de lumière.
fr.B: Rien de surprenant : Satan lui-même se fait passer pour un ange de lumière.
fr.R: Cela ne devrait pas nous surprendre. Même Satan se donne l’apparence d’un ange brillant venu du ciel.

es.L: Y no [es] de extrañar, porque el mismo Satanás se disfraza de ángel de luz.
es.B: Nada sorprendente: el mismo Satanás se hace pasar por ángel de luz.
es.R: Eso no debería sorprendernos. Incluso Satanás se hace pasar por un ángel brillante del cielo.

sw.L: Na si jambo la kushangaza, kwa maana Shetani mwenyewe anajibadilisha sura [kuwa] malaika wa nuru.
sw.B: Hilo halishangazi: Shetani mwenyewe hujifanya malaika wa nuru.
sw.R: Hilo lisitushangaze. Hata Shetani hujifanya aonekane kama malaika anayeng'aa kutoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary of God and his people
decisions.reason: Σατανᾶς comes from the Hebrew word for adversary or accuser. Paul has already warned that Satan schemes against the church (2:11) and blinds unbelievers (4:4, where he is "the god of this age").

decisions.choice: an angel of light: a messenger who seems to come from God
decisions.reason: Light belongs to God and his presence (4:6; 1 John 1:5), so an angel of light is one who seems to bring a message from God. Some Jewish writings of the time, such as the Life of Adam and Eve, tell of Satan taking on the brightness of an angel to deceive Eve, which ties this verse to verse 3. Paul does not need that story, however, to make his point: deception looks like the truth.

decisions.choice: a shining angel from heaven
decisions.reason: Readable says what "of light" suggests: an angel who seems to come from God (m2).

source.text: οὐ μέγα οὖν εἰ καὶ οἱ διάκονοι αὐτοῦ μετασχηματίζονται ὡς διάκονοι δικαιοσύνης, ὧν τὸ τέλος ἔσται κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Not great therefore if also the servants of him disguise themselves as servants of righteousness, of whom the end will be according to the works of them.

en.L: [It is] no great [thing], then, if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness; their end will be according to their works.
en.B: So it is no great thing if his servants also pass themselves off as servants of righteousness. Their end will match what they have done.
en.R: So it is not strange that his servants also pretend to be servants who bring righteousness. In the end they will get what their actions deserve.

fr.L: [Ce n’est] donc pas grand-chose si ses serviteurs aussi se déguisent en serviteurs de justice ; leur fin sera selon leurs œuvres.
fr.B: Ce n’est donc pas grand-chose si ses serviteurs aussi se font passer pour des serviteurs de la justice. Leur fin sera à la mesure de ce qu’ils ont fait.
fr.R: Alors, il n’est pas étrange que ses serviteurs aussi fassent semblant d’être des serviteurs qui apportent la justice. À la fin, ils recevront ce que leurs actions méritent.

es.L: No [es] gran cosa, pues, si también sus servidores se disfrazan de servidores de justicia; su fin será conforme a sus obras.
es.B: Así que no es nada extraño que sus servidores también se hagan pasar por servidores de la justicia. Su final corresponderá a lo que han hecho.
es.R: Así que no es raro que sus servidores también finjan ser servidores que traen justicia. Al final recibirán lo que merecen sus acciones.

sw.L: Basi si jambo kubwa ikiwa watumishi wake nao wanajibadilisha sura kama watumishi wa haki; mwisho wao utakuwa kwa kadiri ya matendo yao.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo si jambo kubwa ikiwa watumishi wake pia hujifanya watumishi wa haki. Mwisho wao utalingana na yale waliyotenda.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo si ajabu kwamba watumishi wake pia hujifanya kuwa watumishi wanaoleta haki. Mwishowe watapata kile ambacho matendo yao yanastahili.

decisions.choice: servants of righteousness: those who serve God's work of making people right with him
alternatives: people who simply live good lives
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνης here recalls 3:9, where Paul calls his work "the ministry of righteousness", and 5:21. The rivals present themselves as ministers of God's saving righteousness while they serve Satan. διάκονοι is the word Paul uses for himself as a servant (3:6; 6:4), and he will claim it again in verse 23.

decisions.choice: their end will match their works: God's judgment
decisions.reason: Everyone will receive what is due for what they have done (5:10; Romans 2:6). Paul leaves the rivals' end to God.

decisions.choice: servants who bring righteousness
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of servants they claim to be (m1) and keeps the key word "righteousness".

source.text: Πάλιν λέγω, μή τίς με δόξῃ ἄφρονα εἶναι εἰ δὲ μή γε, κἂν ὡς ἄφρονα δέξασθέ με, ἵνα κἀγὼ μικρόν τι καυχήσωμαι·

records.literal_gloss: Again I say, not anyone me should think a fool to be; if but not indeed, even if as a fool receive me, so that I too a little something may boast;

en.L: I say again, let no one think me to be a fool; but if [you do], [then] receive me even as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
en.B: Once more I say it: nobody should think I am a fool. Otherwise, welcome me even as a fool, so that I can boast a little too.
en.R: Let me say it again. I do not want anyone to think I am a fool. But if you do think so, then accept me the way you would accept a fool. Then I can boast a little too, as the others do.

fr.L: Je le dis encore : que personne ne me prenne pour un insensé ; sinon, recevez-moi même comme un insensé, afin que moi aussi je me vante un peu.
fr.B: Je le répète : que personne ne pense que je suis un insensé. Sinon, accueillez-moi même comme un insensé, pour que je puisse, moi aussi, me vanter un peu.
fr.R: Je le redis. Je ne veux pas que quelqu’un pense que je suis un insensé. Mais si vous le pensez, alors acceptez-moi comme vous accepteriez un insensé. Alors je pourrai me vanter un peu, moi aussi, comme les autres le font.

es.L: Otra vez digo: que nadie piense que soy insensato; pero si no, {{plural_you:recíbanme|recibidme}} aunque sea como a insensato, para que también yo me gloríe un poco.
es.B: Lo repito: nadie debe pensar que soy un insensato. Pero si lo {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}}, {{plural_you:acójanme|acogedme}} aunque sea como a un insensato, para que yo también pueda gloriarme un poco.
es.R: {{plural_you:Déjenme|Dejadme}} decirlo otra vez. No quiero que nadie piense que soy un tonto. Pero si {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que lo soy, {{plural_you:acéptenme|aceptadme}} como {{plural_you:aceptarían|aceptaríais}} a un tonto. Así yo también podré gloriarme un poco, como hacen los otros.

sw.L: Nasema tena, mtu yeyote asinidhanie kuwa mpumbavu; lakini kama sivyo, nipokeeni hata kama mpumbavu, ili mimi nami nijivune kidogo.
sw.B: Nasema tena: mtu yeyote asidhani kwamba mimi ni mpumbavu. La sivyo, nikaribisheni hata kama mpumbavu, ili nami nipate kujivuna kidogo.
sw.R: Acheni niseme tena. Sitaki mtu yeyote adhani kwamba mimi ni mpumbavu. Lakini mkidhani hivyo, basi nipokeeni kama mnavyompokea mpumbavu. Ndipo nami nitaweza kujivuna kidogo, kama wengine wanavyofanya.

decisions.choice: fool: someone without good sense
decisions.reason: ἄφρονα belongs with ἀφροσύνη (verse 1; see the decision there). Paul is not a fool, but the boasting the situation forces on him is the kind of thing a fool does. So he asks to be received as a fool, and he speaks the part. It is not the word for the foolishness of the cross in 1 Corinthians 1-3.

decisions.choice: otherwise: if you do think me a fool
decisions.reason: εἰ δὲ μή γε is a fixed phrase meaning "but if not, otherwise", and κἂν means "at least, even if only": if they insist on taking him for a fool, they should at least give him a fool's hearing.

decisions.choice: I too: as the rivals do
decisions.reason: κἀγὼ ("I too") sets Paul beside the rivals, who boast (verses 12 and 18).

decisions.choice: as the others do
decisions.reason: Readable says who the others are (m3).

source.text: ὃ λαλῶ οὐ κατὰ κύριον λαλῶ, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ, ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ὑποστάσει τῆς καυχήσεως.

records.literal_gloss: What I speak not according to [the] Lord I speak, but as in foolishness, in this the confidence of the boasting.

en.L: What I am speaking, I am not speaking according to [the] Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
en.B: What I say with this confidence in boasting is not said in the Lord's way, but as it were in foolishness.
en.R: When I boast so confidently like this, I am not talking the way the Lord would talk. I am talking like a fool.

fr.L: Ce que je dis, je ne le dis pas selon le Seigneur, mais comme dans la folie, dans cette assurance de vantardise.
fr.B: Ce que je dis avec cette assurance quand je me vante, je ne le dis pas à la manière du Seigneur, mais pour ainsi dire dans la folie.
fr.R: Quand je me vante avec autant d’assurance, je ne parle pas comme le Seigneur parlerait. Je parle comme un insensé.

es.L: Lo que hablo, no lo hablo según [el] Señor, sino como en insensatez, en esta confianza de gloriarme.
es.B: Lo que digo con esta confianza al gloriarme no lo digo a la manera del Señor, sino como si fuera en insensatez.
es.R: Cuando me glorío con tanta seguridad, no estoy hablando como hablaría el Señor. Estoy hablando como un tonto.

sw.L: Ninachosema, sisemi kwa kufuata Bwana, bali kama katika upumbavu, katika uhakika huu wa kujivuna.
sw.B: Ninachosema kwa uhakika huu wa kujivuna sikisemi kwa njia ya Bwana, bali kana kwamba ni katika upumbavu.
sw.R: Ninapojivuna kwa uhakika namna hii, sizungumzi jinsi Bwana angezungumza. Nazungumza kama mpumbavu.

decisions.choice: not according to the Lord: not in the way the Lord acts and speaks
alternatives: not inspired by the Lord, not part of Scripture
decisions.reason: κατὰ κύριον means in keeping with the Lord, his humble and gentle ways (10:1) and his rule that whoever boasts should boast in the Lord (10:17). Paul admits that boasting about himself does not match the Lord's way. He is not saying that these words lack the Lord's authority.

decisions.choice: confidence: this bold, self-assured kind of boasting
alternatives: the matter, the subject of boasting
decisions.reason: ὑποστάσει can mean the confidence a person has or the subject in hand. Paul uses the same phrase in 9:4 for a confidence he might be ashamed of. Here it is the bold self-confidence of the boaster whose part he plays.

decisions.choice: like a fool
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "fool" and makes the comparison plain.

decisions.choice: cette assurance de vantardise (L)
decisions.reason: Here the boasting is the fool's kind, not according to the Lord (m1, m2), so Literal uses the pejorative noun "vantardise", as the drafts of chapters 12-13 do.

source.text: ἐπεὶ πολλοὶ καυχῶνται κατὰ σάρκα, κἀγὼ καυχήσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: Since many boast according to flesh, I too will boast.

en.L: Since many boast according to [the] flesh, I too will boast.
en.B: Since many are boasting by merely human standards, I will boast too.
en.R: Many people boast the way selfish people do, so I will boast too.

fr.L: Puisque beaucoup se vantent selon la chair, moi aussi je me vanterai.
fr.B: Puisque beaucoup se vantent selon des critères purement humains, je me vanterai moi aussi.
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens se vantent comme le font les gens égoïstes, alors je vais me vanter moi aussi.

es.L: Puesto que muchos se glorían según [la] carne, también yo me gloriaré.
es.B: Ya que muchos se glorían con criterios meramente humanos, yo también me gloriaré.
es.R: Mucha gente se gloría de la manera en que lo hace la gente egoísta, así que yo también me gloriaré.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa wengi wanajivuna kwa kufuata mwili, mimi nami nitajivuna.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa wengi wanajivuna kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu tu, nami nitajivuna.
sw.R: Watu wengi wanajivuna kama watu wenye ubinafsi, kwa hiyo nami nitajivuna.

decisions.choice: according to the flesh: by merely human standards
decisions.reason: κατὰ σάρκα means judged by what is merely human: family, nation, achievements and outward show, which Paul lists in verses 22-23, as he does in Philippians 3:4-6. The "many" are the rivals. Paul has said that he does not wage war according to the flesh (10:2-3); now, in his fool's speech, he will boast on their terms for a while.

decisions.choice: by merely human standards (B); the way selfish people do (R)
decisions.reason: "Flesh" suggests the body to a modern reader. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m1), in the same words as 10:2.

source.text: ἡδέως γὰρ ἀνέχεσθε τῶν ἀφρόνων φρόνιμοι ὄντες·

records.literal_gloss: Gladly for you put up with the fools wise being;

en.L: For you gladly put up with fools, being wise [yourselves].
en.B: You are wise people, after all, and so you happily bear with fools!
en.R: You are so wise! That is why you are happy to put up with fools.

fr.L: Car vous supportez volontiers les insensés, vous qui êtes sensés.
fr.B: Vous êtes des gens sensés, après tout, et c’est pourquoi vous supportez avec plaisir les insensés !
fr.R: Vous êtes si sages ! C’est pour cela que vous êtes contents de supporter les insensés.

es.L: Porque con gusto {{plural_you:toleran|toleráis}} a los insensatos, siendo [{{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}] sensatos.
es.B: ¡Al fin y al cabo, {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} tan sensatos que {{plural_you:aguantan|aguantáis}} con gusto a los insensatos!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} tan sensatos! Por eso {{plural_you:aguantan|aguantáis}} con gusto a los tontos.

sw.L: Kwa maana mnawavumilia wapumbavu kwa furaha, mkiwa wenye busara [ninyi wenyewe].
sw.B: Ninyi ni watu wenye busara hata hivyo, na kwa hiyo mnawavumilia wapumbavu kwa furaha!
sw.R: Ninyi mna busara sana! Ndiyo maana mnafurahi kuwavumilia wapumbavu.

decisions.choice: irony: the Corinthians think themselves wise
decisions.reason: Paul does not mean that they are wise. As in 1 Corinthians 4:10 ("you are wise in Christ"), he turns their opinion of themselves against them: people so wise ought not to welcome fools, yet they welcome the rivals, and so they can welcome Paul's foolishness too. φρόνιμοι ("wise, sensible") and ἀφρόνων ("fools, senseless") are a play on words in the Greek.

decisions.choice: les insensés ... sensés (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Greek sets the fools against the wise in a single phrase of irony (m1); "insensés" and "sensés" let French keep that play. Readable says "sages", as the English says "wise".

decisions.choice: sensatos
decisions.reason: Paul sets the Corinthians' good sense against the fools with two words from one root, ironically. "Sensatos" against "insensatos" keeps that play in Spanish; "sabios" is kept for the wisdom word of 1 Corinthians 1-3.

source.text: ἀνέχεσθε γὰρ εἴ τις ὑμᾶς καταδουλοῖ, εἴ τις κατεσθίει, εἴ τις λαμβάνει, εἴ τις ἐπαίρεται, εἴ τις εἰς πρόσωπον ὑμᾶς δέρει.

records.literal_gloss: You put up with for if someone you enslaves, if someone devours, if someone takes, if someone exalts himself, if someone into [the] face you strikes.

en.L: For you put up with [it] if someone enslaves you, if someone devours [you], if someone takes [you], if someone is lifted up [over you], if someone strikes you in the face.
en.B: Indeed you put up with it if someone holds you in bondage, if someone eats you up, if someone takes you in, if someone lords it over you, if someone hits you in the face.
en.R: You let people make you serve them. You let them take everything you have. You let them trick you. You let them act as if they are better than you. You even let them slap you in the face!

fr.L: Car vous [le] supportez, si quelqu’un vous asservit, si quelqu’un [vous] dévore, si quelqu’un [vous] prend, si quelqu’un s’élève [au-dessus de vous], si quelqu’un vous frappe au visage.
fr.B: Oui, vous le supportez si quelqu’un vous tient en servitude, si quelqu’un vous dévore, si quelqu’un vous prend au piège, si quelqu’un vous traite de haut, si quelqu’un vous frappe au visage.
fr.R: Vous laissez des gens vous obliger à les servir. Vous les laissez prendre tout ce que vous avez. Vous les laissez vous tromper. Vous les laissez agir comme s’ils valaient mieux que vous. Vous les laissez même vous gifler !

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:toleran|toleráis}} si alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} esclaviza, si alguien [{{plural_you:los|os}}] devora, si alguien [{{plural_you:los|os}}] atrapa, si alguien se enaltece [sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}], si alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} golpea en la cara.
es.B: En efecto, lo {{plural_you:aguantan|aguantáis}} si alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} reduce a servidumbre, si alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} devora, si alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} atrapa con engaños, si alguien se pone por encima de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si alguien {{plural_you:les|os}} pega en la cara.
es.R: {{plural_you:Permiten|Permitís}} que otros {{plural_you:los|os}} hagan sus siervos. {{plural_you:Permiten|Permitís}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} quiten todo lo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}. {{plural_you:Permiten|Permitís}} que {{plural_you:los|os}} engañen. {{plural_you:Permiten|Permitís}} que actúen como si fueran mejores que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¡Hasta {{plural_you:permiten|permitís}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} den bofetadas!

sw.L: Kwa maana mnavumilia mtu akiwafanya watumwa, mtu akiwameza, mtu akiwachukua, mtu akijiinua, mtu akiwapiga usoni.
sw.B: Naam, mnavumilia mtu akiwatia utumwani, mtu akiwala mali, mtu akiwanasa, mtu akijifanya bwana juu yenu, mtu akiwapiga usoni.
sw.R: Mnawaacha watu wawafanye muwatumikie. Mnawaacha wachukue kila kitu mlicho nacho. Mnawaacha wawadanganye. Mnawaacha wajifanye kuwa bora kuliko ninyi. Hata mnawaacha wawapige makofi usoni!

decisions.choice: five kinds of abuse by the rivals: control, exploiting, trapping, arrogance, insult
decisions.reason: καταδουλοῖ is to reduce to slavery, to bring under someone's control (Galatians 2:4). κατεσθίει is to eat up, to exploit people's resources (Mark 12:40). λαμβάνει, here without an object, means to catch or take advantage of, as in 12:16, where Paul is accused of catching the Corinthians by a trick. ἐπαίρεται is to lift oneself up, to act arrogantly (10:5). Everything the rivals do is the opposite of Paul, who would not burden anyone (verse 9).

decisions.choice: struck in the face: a deep insult
alternatives: a figure of speech for humiliating treatment only
decisions.reason: A slap in the face was the classic insult (Matthew 5:39; Acts 23:2). Paul may mean that the rivals actually struck people, or he may use the picture for the contempt with which they treated the church.

decisions.choice: take everything you have; trick you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1).

decisions.choice: holds you in bondage (B); make you serve them (R)
decisions.reason: "Enslave" becomes "hold in bondage" in Balanced and "make ... serve" in Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the rivals bring them under their control, and Literal keeps "enslaves".

decisions.choice: akiwafanya watumwa (L); akiwatia utumwani (B)
decisions.reason: Being made slaves is itself the point, so Literal and Balanced keep the slavery words "watumwa" and "utumwa", as the English Balanced says "bondage"; Readable says "muwatumikie" (that you serve them), as the English Readable does.

source.text: κατὰ ἀτιμίαν λέγω, ὡς ὅτι ἡμεῖς ἠσθενήκαμεν· ἐν ᾧ δ’ ἄν τις τολμᾷ, ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ λέγω, τολμῶ κἀγώ.

records.literal_gloss: According to shame I say, as that we have been weak; in whatever but anyone dares, in foolishness I speak, dare also I.

en.L: I say [it] to [our] shame: we have been weak! But in whatever anyone dares, I am speaking in foolishness, I too dare.
en.B: I must say, to our shame, that we have been far too weak to act like that! But whatever anyone else dares to boast of (I am talking in foolishness), I dare to boast of it too.
en.R: I am ashamed to admit it, but we were not strong enough to treat you like that! But if others dare to boast about something, then I dare to boast about it too. (I am talking like a fool.)

fr.L: Je le dis à [notre] honte : nous avons été faibles ! Mais là où quelqu’un ose (je parle dans la folie), moi aussi j’ose.
fr.B: Je dois le dire, à notre honte : nous avons été bien trop faibles pour agir ainsi ! Mais tout ce dont un autre ose se vanter (je parle dans la folie), j’ose m’en vanter moi aussi.
fr.R: J’ai honte de l’avouer, mais nous n’avons pas été assez forts pour vous traiter comme cela ! Mais si d’autres osent se vanter de quelque chose, alors moi aussi j’ose m’en vanter. (Je parle comme un insensé.)

es.L: Para [nuestra] vergüenza lo digo: ¡nosotros hemos sido débiles! Pero en aquello en que cualquiera se atreva (hablo con insensatez), también yo me atrevo.
es.B: Tengo que decirlo, para vergüenza nuestra: ¡hemos sido demasiado débiles para actuar así! Pero de cualquier cosa de la que otro se atreva a gloriarse (hablo como un insensato), yo también me atrevo a gloriarme.
es.R: Me da vergüenza admitirlo, pero ¡no fuimos lo bastante fuertes para {{plural_you:tratarlos|trataros}} así! Pero si otros se atreven a gloriarse de algo, yo también me atrevo a gloriarme de eso. (Estoy hablando como un tonto.)

sw.L: Nasema [hili] kwa aibu [yetu]: sisi tumekuwa dhaifu! Lakini katika lolote ambalo mtu anathubutu, nasema katika upumbavu, mimi nami nathubutu.
sw.B: Lazima niseme, kwa aibu yetu, kwamba tulikuwa dhaifu mno kutenda hivyo! Lakini chochote ambacho mtu mwingine anathubutu kujivunia (nazungumza katika upumbavu), nami nathubutu kukijivunia.
sw.R: Naona aibu kukubali, lakini hatukuwa na nguvu za kuwatendea hivyo! Lakini wengine wakithubutu kujivunia jambo fulani, basi nami nathubutu kulijivunia. (Nazungumza kama mpumbavu.)

decisions.choice: mock shame: we were too weak to treat you as the rivals do
alternatives: Paul repeats the charge his critics make, that he is weak
decisions.reason: Paul says with irony that he must confess, to his shame, a weakness: he never abused the Corinthians as the rivals do (verse 20). ὡς ὅτι can mean "as if", reporting how others see it, so the clause may also echo the charge that he is weak (10:10). Either way the irony is the same: what they call weakness is his refusal to exploit them.

decisions.choice: in whatever anyone dares: whatever the rivals are bold enough to claim
decisions.reason: τολμᾷ is to dare, to be bold, Paul's word in 10:2 and 10:12. The claims meant are those he is about to list (verses 22-23), so the boldness is boasting. The words "I am speaking in foolishness" break in as an aside.

decisions.choice: dares to boast of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the daring is (m2). "Boast" is supplied, so Literal does not have it. "Dare" matches 10:2 and 10:12.

decisions.reason: Paul has called the rivals servants of Satan who pose as servants of righteousness (verses 13-15). Here he takes up their claim to be servants of Christ without granting it, to show that by the measure of service he outdoes them. διάκονοι is the word of 3:6 and 6:4.

source.text: παραφρονῶν λαλῶ, ὑπὲρ ἐγώ· ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως, ἐν φυλακαῖς περισσοτέρως, ἐν πληγαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως, ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις·

records.literal_gloss: Being out of my mind I speak, more I; in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in blows beyond measure, in deaths often;

en.L: I speak as one out of [my] mind: I [am] more; in labors far more, in prisons far more, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths often.
en.B: I am talking as if I had lost my mind, but I am a better one: with far more labors, far more imprisonments, beatings past counting, and brushes with death again and again.
en.R: I am talking like someone who has gone crazy, but I serve {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} even more than they do. I have worked much harder. I have been in prison more often. I have been beaten more times than I can count. Many times I almost died.

fr.L: Je parle en homme qui a perdu la raison : moi plus [encore] ; dans les travaux bien plus, dans les prisons bien plus, sous les coups au-delà de toute mesure, dans [des dangers de] mort souvent.
fr.B: Je parle comme si j’avais perdu la raison, mais je le suis plus qu’eux : bien plus de travaux, bien plus d’emprisonnements, des coups sans nombre, des dangers de mort à maintes reprises.
fr.R: Je parle comme quelqu’un qui est devenu fou, mais je sers le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} encore plus qu’eux. J’ai travaillé beaucoup plus dur. J’ai été en prison plus souvent. J’ai été battu plus de fois que je ne peux compter. Bien des fois, j’ai failli mourir.

es.L: Hablo como fuera de mí: yo [lo soy] más; en trabajos, mucho más; en cárceles, mucho más; en azotes, sin medida; en muertes, muchas veces.
es.B: Hablo como si hubiera perdido el juicio, pero yo lo soy más: con muchos más trabajos, muchas más veces en la cárcel, con azotes sin número, y muchas veces al borde de la muerte.
es.R: Estoy hablando como un loco, pero yo sirvo {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} aún más que ellos. He trabajado mucho más. He estado en la cárcel más veces. Me han azotado más veces de las que puedo contar. Muchas veces estuve a punto de morir.

sw.L: Nasema kama mwenye wazimu: mimi zaidi; katika kazi ngumu kwa wingi zaidi, katika vifungo kwa wingi zaidi, katika mapigo kupita kiasi, katika vifo mara nyingi.
sw.B: Nazungumza kana kwamba nimepatwa na wazimu, lakini mimi ni mtumishi bora zaidi: nimefanya kazi ngumu zaidi sana, nimefungwa gerezani mara nyingi zaidi, nimepigwa mara zisizohesabika, na mara kwa mara nimekaribia kifo.
sw.R: Nazungumza kama mtu aliyechanganyikiwa akili, lakini mimi namtumikia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} hata kuliko wao. Nimefanya kazi kwa bidii zaidi. Nimefungwa gerezani mara nyingi zaidi. Nimepigwa mara nyingi kuliko ninavyoweza kuhesabu. Mara nyingi nilikaribia kufa.

decisions.choice: out of my mind: beyond foolishness, like a madman
decisions.reason: παραφρονῶν is stronger than the foolishness of verses 1, 16-17 and 21: it means to be beside oneself, insane. To compare himself with the rivals as their better is, Paul says, madness.

decisions.choice: I more: I am a servant of Christ even more than they
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ ἐγώ ("more, I") is compressed. Paul does not deny the title but claims more right to it, and the proof is not success but suffering.

decisions.choice: deaths: times of mortal danger
decisions.reason: θανάτοις, plural, means situations in which he nearly died (1:9-10; 4:11).

decisions.choice: imprisonments and beatings: only some are recorded in Acts
decisions.reason: Before this letter Acts records one imprisonment, at Philippi, with a beating (Acts 16:22-24); Paul refers to others the record does not include. The list is the fullest account of his sufferings in the New Testament (compare 6:4-5; 1 Corinthians 4:9-13).

decisions.choice: with far more labors, far more imprisonments, beatings past counting
alternatives: I have worked much harder, been in prison more
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the list form of the Greek, a string of phrases without verbs, so that its rhythm can be heard.

decisions.choice: I serve Christ even more than they do
decisions.reason: Readable completes Paul's compressed claim (m2).

decisions.choice: dans [des dangers de] mort (L)
decisions.reason: French "des morts" in the plural would mean dead people; Literal supplies the words that say what the Greek plural means (m3).

decisions.choice: fuera de mí (L); como si hubiera perdido el juicio (B); como un loco (R)
decisions.reason: This verb is stronger than the fool words of chapters 11-12: being out of one's mind. Spanish keeps it apart from "insensato", as the English says "out of my mind".

decisions.choice: kama mwenye wazimu (L); nimepatwa na wazimu (B)
decisions.reason: This is a stronger word than "mpumbavu" (fool): beyond foolishness, like a madman (meaning decision). "Kurukwa na akili" is kept for a different verb in 5:13.
