records.literal_gloss: By Jews five times forty less one I received, \v 25 three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day in the deep I have spent;

en.L: From [the] Jews five times I received forty [lashes] less one; \v 25 three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, a night and a day I have spent in the deep.
en.B: Five times the Jewish authorities gave me the forty lashes less one. \v 25 Three times I was flogged with rods; once I was stoned; three times my ship was wrecked; a night and a day I have spent out on the deep.
en.R: Five times the Jewish leaders had me whipped thirty-nine times. \v 25 Three times I was beaten with rods. Once people threw stones at me to kill me. Three times I was on a ship that was wrecked. Once I spent a whole night and day floating in the sea.

fr.L: Des Juifs, j’ai reçu cinq fois quarante [coups] moins un ; \v 25 trois fois j’ai été battu de verges, une fois j’ai été lapidé, trois fois j’ai fait naufrage, j’ai passé une nuit et un jour dans l’abîme.
fr.B: Cinq fois, les autorités juives m’ont infligé les quarante coups moins un. \v 25 Trois fois, j’ai été battu de verges ; une fois, j’ai été lapidé ; trois fois, j’ai fait naufrage ; j’ai passé une nuit et un jour en pleine mer.
fr.R: Cinq fois, les chefs juifs m’ont fait donner trente-neuf coups de fouet. \v 25 Trois fois, j’ai été battu avec des bâtons. Une fois, des gens m’ont jeté des pierres pour me tuer. Trois fois, j’étais sur un bateau qui a fait naufrage. Une fois, j’ai passé toute une nuit et toute une journée à flotter dans la mer.

es.L: De [los] judíos cinco veces recibí cuarenta [azotes] menos uno; \v 25 tres veces fui golpeado con varas, una vez fui apedreado, tres veces naufragué, una noche y un día he pasado en lo profundo [del mar].
es.B: Cinco veces las autoridades judías me dieron los cuarenta azotes menos uno. \v 25 Tres veces me azotaron con varas; una vez me apedrearon; tres veces naufragué; una noche y un día los pasé a la deriva en alta mar.
es.R: Cinco veces los líderes judíos hicieron que me dieran treinta y nueve latigazos. \v 25 Tres veces me golpearon con varas. Una vez me tiraron piedras para matarme. Tres veces iba en un barco que naufragó. Una vez pasé una noche y un día enteros flotando en el mar.

sw.L: Kutoka kwa Wayahudi nilipokea mara tano [viboko] arobaini kasoro kimoja; \v 25 mara tatu nilichapwa kwa fimbo, mara moja nilipigwa mawe, mara tatu meli niliyosafiria ilivunjika, usiku na mchana [mzima] nimekuwa katika bahari kuu.
sw.B: Mara tano viongozi wa Wayahudi walinichapa viboko arobaini kasoro kimoja. \v 25 Mara tatu nilichapwa kwa fimbo; mara moja nilipigwa mawe; mara tatu meli yangu ilivunjika; usiku mmoja na mchana mmoja nimekaa majini katika bahari kuu.
sw.R: Mara tano viongozi wa Wayahudi waliamuru nichapwe viboko thelathini na tisa. \v 25 Mara tatu nilipigwa kwa fimbo. Mara moja watu walinitupia mawe ili waniue. Mara tatu nilikuwa ndani ya meli iliyovunjika. Wakati mmoja nilikaa usiku mzima na mchana mzima nikielea baharini.

decisions.choice: forty lashes less one: the synagogue punishment of thirty-nine strokes
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 25:3 limits a flogging to forty strokes. Jewish practice stopped at thirty-nine so as not to break the law by miscounting, as the later rules of the Mishnah also show. The punishment was given by synagogue authorities to Jews, so Paul kept going to the synagogues as a member of his people and accepted their discipline. Acts records none of these five floggings.

decisions.choice: beaten with rods: a Roman punishment carried out by city officials
decisions.reason: ἐραβδίσθην is the punishment given by the attendants of Roman magistrates, who carried rods. At Philippi Paul and Silas were beaten this way, though Paul was a Roman citizen (Acts 16:22-23, 37). The other two occasions are not recorded.

decisions.choice: stoned once: at Lystra
decisions.reason: At Lystra a crowd stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead (Acts 14:19).

decisions.choice: shipwrecked three times, a full day and night adrift
decisions.reason: None of these shipwrecks is in Acts; the wreck on the way to Rome (Acts 27) came later. νυχθήμερον is a night and a day, a full twenty-four hours, and βυθῷ is the deep, the open sea. The perfect πεποίηκα ("I have spent") makes the memory vivid.

decisions.choice: the Jewish authorities (B); the Jewish leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The punishment was given by synagogue authorities (m1); Balanced and Readable say so, so that "the Jews" is not heard as the whole people.

decisions.choice: thirty-nine times
decisions.reason: Readable gives the number plainly (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the Greek way of counting, which recalls the limit of forty in Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level for Paul's list of sufferings (11:23-29)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The list is part of Paul's boasting speech to the readers, not a story told in order, and the Greek itself moves into the perfect ("I have spent"); French uses the passé composé for that. The Damascus story of verses 32-33 is narrated in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: viongozi wa Wayahudi
decisions.reason: The lashes were a synagogue punishment ordered by Jewish authorities (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable say "viongozi wa Wayahudi", the phrase settled in John for the authorities.

records.literal_gloss: In journeys often, in dangers of rivers, in dangers of robbers, in dangers from race, in dangers from Gentiles, in dangers in city, in dangers in wilderness, in dangers in sea, in dangers among false brothers, \v 27 in labor and toil, in sleeplessnesses often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness;

en.L: [On] journeys often, [in] dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from [my own] people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in [the] city, dangers in [the] wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; \v 27 in labor and toil, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
en.B: Again and again I have been on the road, facing dangers from rivers, dangers from bandits, dangers from my own people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the open country, dangers at sea, dangers among false {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; \v 27 in labor and weariness, many nights without sleep, in hunger and thirst, many days going without food, in cold and with too little to wear.
en.R: I have traveled from place to place many times. Rivers have put me in danger, and so have robbers. I have been in danger from my own Jewish people and from people who are not Jews. I have been in danger in cities, in the wild country, and at sea. I have been in danger from false {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, people who pretended to belong to God's family. \v 27 I have worked hard and been worn out. Many nights I could not sleep. I have been hungry and thirsty. Often I have had nothing to eat. I have been cold and did not have enough clothes to keep warm.

fr.L: Souvent en voyage, dans des dangers venant des fleuves, des dangers venant des brigands, des dangers venant de [mon] peuple, des dangers venant des nations, des dangers dans la ville, des dangers dans le désert, des dangers en mer, des dangers parmi de faux {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ; \v 27 dans la peine et le labeur, souvent dans les veilles, dans la faim et la soif, souvent dans les jeûnes, dans le froid et la nudité.
fr.B: Souvent sur les routes, j’ai connu des dangers venant des fleuves, des dangers venant des bandits, des dangers venant de mon propre peuple, des dangers venant des non-Juifs, des dangers dans la ville, des dangers dans la campagne déserte, des dangers en mer, des dangers parmi de faux {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} ; \v 27 j’ai connu le travail et la fatigue, de nombreuses nuits sans sommeil, la faim et la soif, de nombreux jours sans manger, le froid et le manque de vêtements.
fr.R: J’ai voyagé d’un endroit à l’autre bien des fois. Les rivières m’ont mis en danger, et les brigands aussi. J’ai été en danger à cause de mon propre peuple juif et à cause de gens qui ne sont pas juifs. J’ai été en danger dans les villes, dans les régions sauvages et en mer. J’ai été en danger à cause de faux {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, des gens qui faisaient semblant d’appartenir à la famille de Dieu. \v 27 J’ai travaillé dur et j’ai été épuisé. Bien des nuits, je n’ai pas pu dormir. J’ai eu faim et soif. Souvent, je n’ai rien eu à manger. J’ai eu froid et je n’avais pas assez de vêtements pour me tenir chaud.

es.L: En viajes muchas veces, en peligros de ríos, peligros de bandidos, peligros de [mi propio] pueblo, peligros de [los] gentiles, peligros en [la] ciudad, peligros en [el] desierto, peligros en el mar, peligros entre falsos hermanos; \v 27 en trabajo y fatiga, en desvelos muchas veces, en hambre y sed, en ayunos muchas veces, en frío y desnudez.
es.B: Una y otra vez he estado de viaje, enfrentando peligros de ríos, peligros de bandidos, peligros de mi propio pueblo, peligros de los gentiles, peligros en la ciudad, peligros en lugares despoblados, peligros en el mar, peligros entre falsos hermanos; \v 27 en trabajo y cansancio, muchas noches sin dormir, en hambre y sed, muchos días sin comer, en frío y sin ropa suficiente.
es.R: He viajado de un lugar a otro muchas veces. Los ríos me han puesto en peligro, y también los bandidos. He estado en peligro por causa de mi propio pueblo judío y por causa de gente que no es judía. He estado en peligro en las ciudades, en lugares despoblados y en el mar. He estado en peligro por causa de falsos hermanos, gente que fingía pertenecer a la familia de Dios. \v 27 He trabajado duro y he quedado agotado. Muchas noches no pude dormir. He pasado hambre y sed. A menudo no he tenido nada que comer. He pasado frío y no he tenido ropa suficiente para abrigarme.

sw.L: [katika] safari mara nyingi, katika hatari za mito, hatari za wanyang'anyi, hatari kutoka kwa [watu wa] taifa [langu], hatari kutoka kwa watu wa mataifa, hatari mjini, hatari nyikani, hatari baharini, hatari kati ya ndugu wa uongo; \v 27 katika kazi ngumu na uchovu, katika kukesha mara nyingi, katika njaa na kiu, katika kufunga mara nyingi, katika baridi na uchi.
sw.B: Mara kwa mara nimekuwa safarini, nikikabili hatari za mito, hatari za wanyang'anyi, hatari kutoka kwa watu wa taifa langu, hatari kutoka kwa watu wa mataifa, hatari mjini, hatari nyikani, hatari baharini, hatari kati ya ndugu wa uongo; \v 27 katika kazi ngumu na uchovu, usiku mwingi bila usingizi, katika njaa na kiu, siku nyingi bila chakula, katika baridi na bila nguo za kutosha.
sw.R: Nimesafiri kutoka mahali hadi mahali mara nyingi. Mito imenitia hatarini, na wanyang'anyi pia. Nimekuwa hatarini kutoka kwa Wayahudi wenzangu na kutoka kwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Nimekuwa hatarini mijini, jangwani na baharini. Nimekuwa hatarini kutoka kwa ndugu wa uongo, watu waliojifanya kuwa wa familia ya Mungu. \v 27 Nimefanya kazi kwa bidii mpaka nikachoka kabisa. Usiku mwingi sikuweza kulala. Nimekuwa na njaa na kiu. Mara nyingi sikuwa na chakula. Nimekuwa na baridi bila nguo za kutosha kunipa joto.

decisions.choice: the dangers of travel by road and sea
decisions.reason: Paul traveled thousands of miles, mostly on foot. Rivers had few bridges and could flood without warning, and bandits were a known danger on roads through mountains and lonely country. ἐρημίᾳ is uninhabited country, not necessarily desert.

decisions.choice: from my own people, from Gentiles: opposition from Jews and from non-Jews
decisions.reason: γένους ("race") means Paul's own people, the Jews; Acts tells of plots and attacks by Jewish opponents (Acts 9:23, 29; 13:50; 14:19; 17:5) and of trouble stirred up by Gentiles (Acts 16:19-22; 19:23-41).

decisions.choice: false brothers: people who claimed to be fellow believers but were not
decisions.reason: ψευδαδέλφοις is used in Galatians 2:4 of people who slipped into the church to spy on its freedom. It is masculine plural, the ordinary way to speak of a group that may include women as well as men.

decisions.choice: fastings: going without food, perhaps sometimes by choice
alternatives: going without food only because there was none
decisions.reason: νηστείαις usually means fasting. Here it stands next to "hunger and thirst", which suggests something different from simple want, perhaps food given up for the sake of the work; but in this list of hardships it may mean going hungry for lack of time or means, as in 6:5.

decisions.choice: labor and toil, cold and nakedness: hard work, and too little clothing
decisions.reason: κόπῳ and μόχθῳ are a common pair for exhausting work (1 Thessalonians 2:9), as Paul supported himself by his trade. γυμνότητι is not literal nakedness but having too little to wear against the cold (1 Corinthians 4:11).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: False believers of both sexes are meant (m3), so the default is inclusive, with "brothers" as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: dangers ... dangers
alternatives: a single "in danger from" followed by a list
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats its word for danger eight times. Balanced repeats "dangers" each time to keep the rhythm of the list.

decisions.choice: people who pretended to belong to God's family
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word (m3).

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); des gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term sheet for this word where the English says "Gentiles"; "païens" would suggest people without religion. Readable says it in plain words, as the French of Galatians does.

decisions.choice: falsos hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 1:8, Spanish "hermanos" already includes women, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: ndugu wa uongo, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no span where the English has one, and uses the same phrase as Galatians 2:4.

source.text: χωρὶς τῶν παρεκτὸς ἡ ἐπίστασίς μοι ἡ καθ’ ἡμέραν, ἡ μέριμνα πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Apart from the things besides, the pressure on me the daily, the concern of all the churches.

en.L: Apart from the things besides [these], [there is] the daily pressure on me, the concern for all the churches.
en.B: And apart from all these other things, there is what presses on me day after day: my anxious care for all the churches.
en.R: And that is not all. Every day I feel the weight of caring for all the churches.

fr.L: Sans parler du reste, [il y a] ce qui pèse sur moi chaque jour, le souci de toutes les églises.
fr.B: Et en plus de tout le reste, il y a ce qui m’assaille jour après jour : mon inquiétude pour toutes les églises.
fr.R: Et ce n’est pas tout. Chaque jour, je sens le poids du souci que j’ai pour toutes les églises.

es.L: Aparte de las demás cosas, [está] la presión diaria sobre mí, la preocupación por todas las iglesias.
es.B: Y además de todas estas cosas, está lo que pesa sobre mí día tras día: mi preocupación por todas las iglesias.
es.R: Y eso no es todo. Cada día siento el peso de cuidar de todas las iglesias.

sw.L: Mbali na mambo mengine [haya], [kuna] msongo ulio juu yangu kila siku, wasiwasi kwa ajili ya makanisa yote.
sw.B: Na mbali na mambo hayo mengine yote, kuna kile kinachonilemea siku baada ya siku: kuyahangaikia makanisa yote.
sw.R: Na hayo si yote. Kila siku ninahisi uzito wa kuyajali makanisa yote.

decisions.choice: apart from the other things: besides everything not mentioned
decisions.reason: παρεκτὸς can mean "besides, apart from" or "outside". Paul may mean the many other things he has not listed, or the outward troubles just named, set against the inner burden that follows.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "pressure"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have the word for pressure or a crowding in on someone; many later manuscripts have a longer word meaning an attack or rush of people upon him. The sense differs little. The SBLGNT has the first. This description is from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: concern for all the churches: an anxious care for them
decisions.reason: μέριμνα is anxiety or concern. Paul tells the Philippians not to be anxious about anything (Philippians 4:6), but here it is the proper care of one who is responsible for others (1 Corinthians 12:25).

source.text: τίς ἀσθενεῖ, καὶ οὐκ ἀσθενῶ;

records.literal_gloss: Who is weak, and not I am weak?

en.L: Who is weak, and I am not weak?
en.B: Is anyone weak without my feeling weak as well?
en.R: When someone is weak, I feel weak too.

fr.L: Qui est faible, et je ne suis pas faible ?
fr.B: Quelqu’un est-il faible sans que je me sente faible aussi ?
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un est faible, je me sens faible moi aussi.

es.L: ¿Quién es débil, y yo no soy débil?
es.B: ¿Hay alguien débil sin que yo también me sienta débil?
es.R: Cuando alguien es débil, yo me siento débil también.

sw.L: Ni nani aliye dhaifu, nami nisiwe dhaifu?
sw.B: Je, kuna mtu aliye dhaifu bila mimi kujisikia dhaifu pia?
sw.R: Mtu anapokuwa dhaifu, nami najisikia dhaifu.

decisions.choice: weak: any weakness, including weakness of faith or conscience
decisions.reason: ἀσθενεῖ is the word for the weak believers of 1 Corinthians 8:7-13 and 9:22, where Paul became weak to win the weak. Here he shares in the weakness of others. The theme of weakness leads into verse 30.

source.text: τίς σκανδαλίζεται καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ πυροῦμαι;

records.literal_gloss: Who is caused to fall, and not I burn?

en.L: Who is caused to fall, and I do not burn?
en.B: Is anyone made to fall without my burning inside?
en.R: When someone is made to fall into sin, I burn inside.

fr.L: Qui est amené à tomber, et je ne brûle pas ?
fr.B: Quelqu’un est-il amené à tomber sans que je brûle intérieurement ?
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un est entraîné dans le péché, je brûle intérieurement.

es.L: ¿Quién es llevado a caer, y yo no ardo?
es.B: ¿Se hace caer a alguien sin que yo arda por dentro?
es.R: Cuando alguien es llevado a caer en pecado, yo ardo por dentro.

sw.L: Ni nani anayekwazwa, nami nisiungue?
sw.B: Je, kuna mtu anayeangushwa bila moyo wangu kuwaka ndani?
sw.R: Mtu anapoangushwa dhambini, moyo wangu unawaka ndani yangu.

decisions.choice: caused to fall: led into sin
decisions.reason: σκανδαλίζεται is the verb of 1 Corinthians 8:13: to be made to stumble and fall, to be led into sin or away from faith.

decisions.choice: I burn: with distress and indignation
decisions.reason: πυροῦμαι is to be set on fire, here inwardly. It can be indignation against whoever caused the fall, or the pain of sharing the fallen person's distress, or both. The verb is the same as in 1 Corinthians 7:9, where it means burning with desire, which does not fit here.

source.text: Εἰ καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ, τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας μου καυχήσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: If to boast it is necessary, the things of the weakness of me I will boast.

en.L: If it is necessary to boast, I will boast of the things of my weakness.
en.B: If boast I must, my boasting will be about the things that belong to my weakness.
en.R: If I have to boast, I will boast about the ways I am weak.

fr.L: S’il faut se vanter, je me vanterai de ce qui concerne ma faiblesse.
fr.B: S’il faut que je me vante, je me vanterai de ce qui relève de ma faiblesse.
fr.R: Si je dois me vanter, je me vanterai des façons dont je suis faible.

es.L: Si es necesario gloriarse, me gloriaré de las cosas de mi debilidad.
es.B: Si tengo que gloriarme, me gloriaré de lo que tiene que ver con mi debilidad.
es.R: Si tengo que gloriarme, me gloriaré de las maneras en que soy débil.

sw.L: Ikiwa ni lazima kujivuna, nitajivunia mambo ya udhaifu wangu.
sw.B: Ikiwa ni lazima nijivune, nitajivunia mambo yanayohusu udhaifu wangu.
sw.R: Ikiwa ni lazima nijivune, nitajivunia jinsi nilivyo dhaifu.

decisions.choice: boasting of weakness: the turn in Paul's argument
decisions.reason: Paul now says plainly what his list has been doing: he boasts not of strength but of what shows him weak, because in weakness Christ's power is seen (12:5, 9-10). This fits the rule he has taken from Jeremiah 9:23-24: whoever boasts should boast in the Lord (10:17; 1 Corinthians 1:31).

decisions.choice: if I must: boasting forced on him
decisions.reason: δεῖ expresses necessity. The rivals' claims and the Corinthians' doubts force Paul to boast (12:1, 11).

source.text: ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ οἶδεν, ὁ ὢν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.

records.literal_gloss: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus knows, the [one] being blessed into the ages, that not I am lying.

en.L: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus knows, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who is blessed to the ages, that I am not lying.
en.B: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, the one who is blessed for all ages, knows that what I say is no lie.
en.R: God, the Father of the Lord Jesus, knows that I am not lying. God deserves praise forever!

fr.L: Le Dieu et Père du Seigneur Jésus sait, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui est béni pour les siècles, que je ne mens pas.
fr.B: Le Dieu et Père du Seigneur Jésus, celui qui est béni pour toujours, sait que ce que je dis n’est pas un mensonge.
fr.R: Dieu, le Père du Seigneur Jésus, sait que je ne mens pas. Dieu mérite d’être loué pour toujours !

es.L: El Dios y Padre del Señor Jesús, el que es bendito por los siglos, sabe que no miento.
es.B: El Dios y Padre del Señor Jesús, que es bendito por siempre, sabe que lo que digo no es mentira.
es.R: Dios, el Padre del Señor Jesús, sabe que no estoy mintiendo. ¡Dios merece alabanza para siempre!

sw.L: Mungu na Baba wa Bwana Yesu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliyebarikiwa milele, anajua kwamba sisemi uongo.
sw.B: Mungu na Baba wa Bwana Yesu, anayehimidiwa milele, anajua kwamba ninayosema si uongo.
sw.R: Mungu, Baba wa Bwana Yesu, anajua kwamba sisemi uongo. Mungu anastahili kusifiwa milele!

decisions.choice: an oath: God is witness that Paul tells the truth
decisions.reason: Paul calls God as witness to the truth of what he says, as in 1:23, Galatians 1:20 and Romans 9:1. The oath may cover the whole list, or it may introduce the story of Damascus that follows, which might seem hard to believe or might be told against him.

decisions.choice: the one who is blessed forever: God the Father
decisions.reason: ὁ ὢν εὐλογητὸς most naturally refers to God, the subject of the sentence, as in Romans 1:25 and 2 Corinthians 1:3. It is praise: God is the one who is worthy of blessing for all ages.

decisions.choice: God deserves praise forever!
decisions.reason: Readable moves the praise into its own sentence so that the oath stays clear.

decisions.choice: el que es bendito, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Literal writes "he who" with a pronoun setting; Spanish says this with the relative "el que", which is not a personal pronoun, so it takes no span.

decisions.choice: aliyebarikiwa (L); anayehimidiwa (B); anastahili kusifiwa (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:3: Literal keeps the word "bless", Balanced the familiar form for praising God, Readable a plain call to praise.

source.text: ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὁ ἐθνάρχης Ἁρέτα τοῦ βασιλέως ἐφρούρει τὴν πόλιν Δαμασκηνῶν πιάσαι με, καὶ διὰ θυρίδος ἐν σαργάνῃ ἐχαλάσθην διὰ τοῦ τείχους καὶ ἐξέφυγον τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: In Damascus the ethnarch of Aretas the king was guarding the city of [the] Damascenes to seize me, \v 33 and through a window in a basket I was let down through the wall and escaped the hands of him.

en.L: In Damascus the ethnarch of Aretas the king was guarding the city of [the] Damascenes to seize me, \v 33 and through a window I was let down in a basket through the wall, and I escaped his hands.
en.B: In Damascus, the ruler appointed by King Aretas set a watch on the city of the Damascenes to catch me. \v 33 But I was let down through an opening in the wall in a rope basket, and I escaped from his grasp.
en.R: When I was in the city of Damascus, the governor who served King Aretas had guards watching the city so that they could arrest me. \v 33 But friends put me in a big basket and let me down through a window in the city wall. So I got away from him.

fr.L: À Damas, l’ethnarque du roi Arétas gardait la ville des Damascéniens pour se saisir de moi, \v 33 et par une fenêtre, dans une corbeille, je fus descendu le long de la muraille, et j’échappai à ses mains.
fr.B: À Damas, le gouverneur nommé par le roi Arétas fit garder la ville des Damascéniens pour m’arrêter. \v 33 Mais on me descendit dans une corbeille par une ouverture de la muraille, et j’échappai à ses mains.
fr.R: Quand j’étais dans la ville de Damas, le gouverneur qui servait le roi Arétas faisait surveiller la ville par des gardes pour qu’ils m’arrêtent. \v 33 Mais des amis m’ont mis dans une grande corbeille et m’ont fait descendre par une fenêtre dans la muraille de la ville. Ainsi, je lui ai échappé.

es.L: En Damasco el etnarca del rey Aretas vigilaba la ciudad de [los] damascenos para prenderme, \v 33 y por una ventana fui descolgado en una canasta a través del muro, y escapé de sus manos.
es.B: En Damasco, el gobernador nombrado por el rey Aretas puso vigilancia en la ciudad de los damascenos para atraparme. \v 33 Pero me bajaron por una abertura del muro en una canasta de cuerdas, y escapé de sus manos.
es.R: Cuando estaba en la ciudad de Damasco, el gobernador que servía al rey Aretas tenía guardias vigilando la ciudad para arrestarme. \v 33 Pero unos amigos me metieron en una canasta grande y me bajaron por una ventana de la muralla de la ciudad. Así escapé de él.

sw.L: Katika Dameski, mtawala wa mfalme Areta alikuwa akiulinda mji wa Wadameski ili anikamate, \v 33 nami nikateremshwa ndani ya tenga kupitia dirisha katika ukuta, nikatoroka mikononi mwake.
sw.B: Huko Dameski, mtawala aliyewekwa na Mfalme Areta aliweka walinzi juu ya mji wa Wadameski ili anikamate. \v 33 Lakini mimi niliteremshwa ndani ya tenga la kamba kupitia mwanya katika ukuta, nikaponyoka mkononi mwake.
sw.R: Nilipokuwa katika mji wa Dameski, gavana aliyemtumikia Mfalme Areta aliweka walinzi kuulinda mji ili wanikamate. \v 33 Lakini rafiki zangu waliniweka ndani ya kikapu kikubwa, wakanishusha kupitia dirisha katika ukuta wa mji. Ndivyo nilivyowaponyoka.

decisions.choice: Aretas and his ethnarch: the Nabatean king and his official
decisions.reason: Aretas IV was king of the Nabateans, the Arab kingdom east and south of Judea with its capital at Petra, from about 9 BC to AD 40. ἐθνάρχης is a ruler or official over a people or district. Whether he controlled Damascus itself or led the Nabatean community there or watched the city from outside is not known.

decisions.choice: the same escape told in Acts 9:23-25
decisions.reason: Acts 9:23-25 says that Jews in Damascus plotted to kill Paul and watched the gates day and night, and that his disciples let him down through the wall in a basket at night. The two accounts tell the same event from different sides: Paul mentions the king's official, Acts the Jewish plotters; both may have worked together.

decisions.choice: window, basket: an opening in the wall, a large woven or rope basket
decisions.reason: θυρίδος is a small window or opening, perhaps in a house built into the city wall, as Rahab's was (Joshua 2:15). σαργάνῃ is a large basket of woven rope or wicker, big enough to hold a man.

decisions.choice: a humiliating escape, told as a boast of weakness
alternatives: a simple record of danger with no further point
decisions.reason: Paul ends his list of boasts with a moment of helplessness: the apostle lowered in a basket and slipping away in the dark. It illustrates verse 30, boasting of weakness. Readers who knew that the Romans gave a crown to the first soldier up an enemy wall may have heard the irony of an apostle who went down one; whether Paul intended that is not certain.

decisions.choice: friends put me in a big basket
alternatives: I was let down in a basket
decisions.reason: Readable names who lowered Paul, from Acts 9:25, which calls them his disciples (m2).

decisions.choice: the ruler appointed by King Aretas
decisions.reason: "Ethnarch" is not common modern English; Balanced describes the office (m1). Literal keeps the Greek title.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je fus descendu", "j’échappai"); passé composé at Readable ("je lui ai échappé")
decisions.reason: Unlike the list of verses 23-29, these verses tell one event in order, a short narrative inside the letter; the style guide has such narration follow section 3, as Paul's travels in Galatians 1-2 do.

decisions.choice: tenga (L, B); kikapu kikubwa (R)
decisions.reason: "Tenga" is a large woven basket, the kind the meaning decision describes; Readable says "kikapu kikubwa" (big basket), the words Swahili Acts 9:25 uses for the same escape.

decisions.choice: Areta; mtawala (L, B); gavana (R)
decisions.reason: The king's name in its Swahili form, "Areta". "Mtawala" (ruler) is the plain word for his official; Readable says "gavana", as the English Readable says governor.
